{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-10-12, on a skill rewording that took ~1 hour to merge: "reflow2 should be able to use in memory BTreeMaps versus the full rocksdb build - I would say that unless rocksdb is being changed itself, that any CI checks use the BTreeMaps option."

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE: the core already has an in-memory backend behind the six-function KvBackend seam (moved HashMap → BTreeMap, chg:the-memory-backend-keeps-its-keys-ordered), and CI's "core gates (no RocksDB)" job already runs the core suite without RocksDB in about two minutes. This is option G of dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds ("feature-gate it out of the builds that do not need it"); the 2026-09-11 ruling there rejected SWAPPING the production engine, not testing on the in-memory one, so this does not reopen it. Production stays RocksDB either way.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) Anthony's: every CI check runs on the in-memory backend unless the diff touches the store (backend, RocksDB options, Cargo's rocksdb pin); a store change runs the RocksDB job too.
(b) The same for pull requests, plus the RocksDB job on every merge to main and always before a cut, so a RocksDB-only regression is caught within one merge rather than never.
(c) Keep testing on RocksDB but stop paying its C++ compile: a prebuilt or cached librocksdb for CI, and a compiler cache (sccache) shared across local worktrees, which unlike a shared target directory cannot build another branch's code.

WHAT EACH COSTS, as far as is known without measuring: (c) is the cheapest and changes nothing about what is tested, but it only helps if RocksDB's compile is actually the paid cost; on 2026-08-24 the long waits were reflow2's own crates recompiling while RocksDB stayed cached, and nobody has split today's 16–25 minute job by step. (a) and (b) are larger: whether reflow2-mcp and its tests build at all without RocksDB is not known, and making them do so is plumbing across a crate.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (1) Fidelity. Users run RocksDB. The real-binary instruments and the design gate exist because some failures appear only in the served binary on a real store (locks, the shared daemon, export from a live store, reopen after restart). (2) The recorded lesson that a workspace build is not the sum of its crates: `-p reflow2-core` plus `-p reflow2-mcp` ran 1,778 tests against `--workspace`'s 1,824, because the workspace unifies the rocksdb feature onto core (fact:a-local-feature-error-was-worked-around-instead-of-read-as-the-ci-contract). Some tests exist only with RocksDB; under (a) they would never run on a PR. (3) "Unless the store changes" is a path list, and a hand-kept path list is the class this project keeps measuring failing; it would have to be derived from the build, not typed.

NOT MEASURED, and the first thing to measure before choosing: how the long job's minutes split between RocksDB's compile, reflow2's own compile, and the tests themselves.
